Turns order-independent transparency on or off. It is off by default, and this is a BlitzLLVM extension: the original sorts see-through entities by their distance (as BlitzLLVM does with it off), which shows when see-through things cross each other or are bigger than they look (leaves in front of a window, smoke sprites that overlap), and the order is wrong for some of the pixels. With it on, everything that is blended (the blend modes alpha, multiply and add of [EntityBlend](EntityBlend), and the layers of textures that blend) is not drawn into the picture in order but added up in four images whose sums do not depend on the order, and one pass over the picture then puts the sums on it: first everything blended by alpha, then the multiplied, then the added.

The alpha is weighted blended order-independent transparency (McGuire and Bavoil, 2013): the colors of all layers at a pixel are averaged with weights that favor the layers that are near, and the opacity is that of all layers together. That is approximate: it is what the layers look like on average, not exactly what the order of the original draws makes, so a picture can differ from the original where layers cross, and a layer that is nearly solid in front of another one shows less of the one behind than it would in the original. Multiply and add are the same sums as in the original (they do not depend on the order). Entities with an [EntityOrder](EntityOrder) other than 0 are still drawn in order, see-through things are still tested against the depth of what is solid and do not write to it, and fading sprites (SpriteDepthFade) work as before. [Dither](Dither) 2 does not blend in the shader while this is on (the sums are half floats and are added to the picture without noise).

It costs four more images the size of the picture (24 bytes per pixel) for each size of picture that is drawn to, and a pass over the picture for each blend mode that was used. It takes effect with the next picture. [HWOrderIndependentTransparency](HWOrderIndependentTransparency) says whether it is available; the environment variable BLITZLLVM_OIT=1 does the same without the command.
@param enable  0 (False) to sort by distance, 1 (True) to add up in any order.
